# Policy rules

Every rule runs on every `dcr check`. A rule has an ID, a severity and a failing-case test.

| Rule | Severity | Checks | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DC001 | high | Contract id is domain.name and matches its file | Ids are how consumers and lineage refer to a contract; a wrong id breaks both silently. |
| DC002 | high | Version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH | Compatibility checks compare versions; a free-form version cannot be compared. |
| DC003 | high | Owner is a registered team | A contract nobody owns is a contract nobody fixes. |
| DC004 | medium | Contract and fields are described | A field without a description is an argument waiting to happen between producer and consumer. |
| DC005 | high | Personal data implies confidential or restricted | Classification drives access control; personal data in an internal table is a leak waiting to be found. |
| DC006 | high | Personal data has a retention limit | Keeping personal data without a limit is a breach of storage limitation waiting for an audit. |
| DC007 | high | Critical contracts promise freshness and completeness | A tier 1 dataset with no SLA cannot be monitored, so nobody finds out when it breaks. |
| DC008 | high | Fields are well formed and live contracts have a key | Duplicate names and missing keys make joins and idempotent loads guesswork. |
| DC009 | high | Consumers are registered teams reading fields that exist | A consumer that names a missing field is already broken or about to be. |
| DC010 | medium | Deprecations are real and not overdue | A deprecation that names no replacement, or sits past its sunset date, teaches consumers to ignore deprecations. |
| DC011 | high | Upstream contracts exist and lineage has no cycles | A cycle means nothing can be the source of truth; a missing upstream means lineage is a guess. |
| DC012 | high | Personal data keeps its label downstream | A column derived from an email address is still personal data; losing the label is how masking gets skipped. |
| DC013 | high | Quality rules are valid and target real fields | A check that cannot run, or runs on nothing, gives false comfort. |
| DC014 | high | Lifecycle status agrees with lineage and consumers | Live data built on a retired source, or a retired contract that is still read, is an outage with a date on it. |
| DC015 | critical | Released versions are immutable and intact | Consumers pin to a released version; if its content can change, the version number means nothing. |
| DC016 | high | Version bump matches the changes | Semantic versions are the signal consumers use to decide whether to look; a wrong bump hides a breaking change. |
| DC017 | low | Contracts under review are labelled draft | A contract that has never been released should say so; 'active' implies consumers can rely on it. |
